### Observed differences

- The choice of successor after activity A02 shifted markedly. In the earlier window, among the outgoing transitions of A02 observed in about 42 of 200 traces, A44 was the most frequent target (about 29 in 100 transitions), followed by A46 (about 17 in 100) and A15 (about 12 in 100). In the later window (about 43 of 200 traces), A46 is the most frequent target (about 30 in 100) while A44 dropped to about 5 in 100 [DIR001].
- Other successor shares moved in the same direction: A15 rose from about 12 to about 19 in 100 and A16 from about 7 to about 12 in 100, while A19 fell from about 10 to about 2 in 100 [DIR001].
- Several successors were observed only in the later window (A14, A41 and A45 at about 5 in 100 each, plus A05, A26, A30 and A35 at about 2 in 100 each), and several only in the earlier window (A04, A18, A25, A27, A32 and A38 at about 2 in 100 each); absence from a window's profile does not show the edge is absent from the process [DIR001].
- A02's own participation was similar in both windows (about 21 of 100 traces before, about 22 of 100 after). The overall distributional difference (cosine dissimilarity 0.33) is larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, but the small shares rest on only one or two observed transitions each [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence
The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one item qualified across 86 tested units, where about 0.43 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so a single item — however unusual it looks — is what a stable process typically produces, and the small transition shares rest on very few observations [DIR001].
